scope: Review of the isolated web modal for a project user deciding whether to invoke simulated Delete project. Evidence is modal.html source and a supplied Chromium observation log produced by someone else. Only the modal component is in scope; no browser tests or implementation changes were performed. Selection was frozen at one checklist and six items before findings.

selected.reason: Directly covers this modal component; all six source item descriptions and tips were read.

excluded.reason: Separate button-component audit is outside the modal-only scope; action clarity is covered by the modal checklist.
Shared foundations are explicitly outside scope; no comprehensive accessibility or conformance assessment is claimed.

items.title: Title
items.reason: “Delete project?” clearly names the decision and action.

items.title: Actionable item
items.evidence: tests/design-guide/fixtures/modal-observations.json: Simulated primary action, callbackRan=true; modal.html button#delete
items.reason: The explicit “Delete project” label identifies the action; the supplied observation establishes that its simulated callback runs. This fixture only sets a boolean.

items.title: Close action
items.location: Open modal; close/cancel, Escape and backdrop dismissal states
items.evidence: tests/design-guide/fixtures/modal-observations.json: Close/cancel controls count=0; Escape dismissal and Backdrop dismissal stillVisible=true
items.reason: The observed states establish no non-destructive way to exit the dialog.
items.impact: A user who declines the simulated action cannot dismiss the dialog through its controls or the exercised dismissal paths.
items.fix: Add a clearly labelled Cancel or Close control that dismisses the dialog without invoking the simulated delete callback; support Escape dismissal.
items.verify: Open the fixture, activate Cancel/Close and press Escape in separate runs; confirm the dialog closes and simulatedDelete is not set.

items.title: Responsiveness
items.evidence: tests/design-guide/fixtures/modal-observations.json: viewport fit observations, modalWidth=640 at both widths, hasHorizontalScroll=false at 1440 and true at 390
items.reason: Desktop fit is established, while the narrow viewport overflows horizontally.
items.impact: Narrow-screen users must scroll horizontally to inspect or operate the dialog.
items.fix: Constrain the modal width to available viewport space with responsive margins and padding; consider full-screen presentation on narrow screens.
items.verify: Recheck at 390px and 1440px, confirming no horizontal overflow and that the title, description and controls remain visible and usable.

items.title: Background change behind modal
items.reason: The implemented full-viewport translucent black backdrop changes the background to focus attention on the modal. This is source evidence, not a personal rendering observation.

items.title: Description
items.reason: The description explains the stated permanent deletion consequence needed for the decision. Actual data deletion is outside this isolated fixture; the callback only sets a boolean.

limitations: Source and supplied observation evidence only; I did not run the browser tests or personally verify runtime rendering.
Runtime observations cover only the listed Chromium states and viewport widths; coverage and verification completion refer only to the six selected checklist items within this evidence boundary.
No full accessibility conformance claim; other UI and shared foundations are outside scope. The Delete action sets a boolean and does not delete actual data.
